I farm the way my mother-in-law taught me and the way everyone around here does. My eleven mu and six fen, I split the same as last year — no reason to change what put grain in the bin.

The eight mu of flat land in back, that's my wheat-maize ground. Wheat goes in October when the cold starts biting, maize straight after we cut the wheat in June. For wheat I buy the improved seed in the red bag from the agent in the market — Old Wang's wife swears by it, and my yield was fine last year. Before ploughing I spread two bags of compound fertilizer per mu, that's the 15-15-15. Then when the wheat turns green in spring I top-dress urea, about one bag for every two mu. Water four times: after sowing, at green-up, at jointing, and when the grain is filling. If I skip the spring water the yield drops and I cannot take that risk. I spray for aphids twice, maybe a third time if they come bad.

Maize goes right into the wheat stubble, no ploughing — the dealer rents a seed drill and it saves my back. Hybrid seed, the one Liu family had good cob size with. One and a half bags compound per mu in the row, urea top-dressed when the maize is knee-high. Water once or twice depending on the rain. Spray once for borer.

My two mu near the road has sandier soil, I keep that in cotton. Bt seed — since we switched we stopped losing the crop to bollworm. Plough it proper in April, one bag compound before planting, urea twice. Water three times from the well. Still need to spray four times for aphids and red spider, Bt only handles the bollworm.

The last mu and six fen, small strip by the ditch, I put mungbean in June after wheat. Mungbean doesn't need feeding — my mother-in-law always said it feeds itself. Just a light scatter of compound, no irrigation, one spray if bugs come. The family eats most of it, some I sell.

I apply a little more fertilizer than the extension people say. I know that. But one bad harvest costs more than a few extra bags of urea, and I have six mouths at home.
